title: Graceful compatibility adapter: non-intrusive behavior flags & migration harness for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: New API behaviors for streaming, tool/function calling payloads, and structured output shaping are rolling out across hosted and dedicated deployments. Several customers run older clients that depend on legacy streaming chunk formats and implicit tool-call fallbacks. We need a low-risk compatibility path that lets us ship stricter/cleaner server-side behavior while offering "non-intrusive" toggles and an adapter layer so legacy clients continue to work without urgent upgrades.

Goals:
- Provide behavior flags scoped per-customer and per-route so we can gate strict changes behind opt-ins and controlled rollouts.
- Implement a compatibility adapter middleware in the runtime that can translate legacy streaming frames and implicit tool-call embeddings to the new structured format at the edge.
- Provide a migration harness and regression replayer that runs historical traffic traces and verifies parity across modes.
- Automate deprecation notices and a phased sunset plan (communication, telemetry, and final cutoff).

Non-goals:
- No permanent support for deprecated behavior; adapter is a transitional shim.
- We will not change client SDKs in this ticket (that is a parallel PM-led effort).

Proposed implementation summary:
1) Behavior flag design: add a three-tier scoping model: global default, organization override, and route-level override. Flags are strings: "compat_streaming_v1", "toolcall_implicit_to_explicit", "structured_output_relaxed_parsing". Flags default to legacy mode for pinned customers with scheduled opt-in windows.
2) Runtime adapter middleware: implement lightweight translation layer in the request path that: a) detects legacy streaming frames and remaps them to new event types with minimal buffering, b) converts implicit tool-call return blobs into new function-calling JSON envelope, c) accepts relaxed structured-output tokens and post-processes to strict schema if requested.
3) Migration harness: extend the regression replayer (ENG-45677) to support recording and replaying streaming sessions and tool-call interactions at token granularity. Provide a small CLI to run a replay against both legacy-emulation and strict server to produce diff reports.
4) Backward-compatibility tests: add unit tests for frame remapping, integration tests for end-to-end streaming and tool-call flows, and a canary pipeline that verifies 99.95th percentile latency impact is <5% when adapter enabled.
5) Rollout: start with internal customers and a small canary cohort, enable route-level flags for test routes, gather telemetry for correctness and cost, then expand to more customers after sign-off.

Success metrics:
- No customer-facing errors attributable to streaming/ tool-call differences during 30-day canary.
- Regression replayer reports 100% functional parity for critical prompts for at least 3 enterprise customers before final deprecation.
- Adapter adds <5% p99 latency overhead in production canary.

Notes on trade-offs and design decisions:
- We prefer an adapter shim over branching runtime codepaths because it centralizes transformation logic and reduces long-term maintenance. This adds some CPU work per-request; we'll measure and add selective sampling to avoid cost blow-up.
- Flags are strings to allow safe future extensions (e.g., v1, v2) without field-type migrations.
- The adapter will not attempt semantic normalization of model outputs; it only re-homes wire-format differences. Full semantic migrations require prompt/temperature tuning outside this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior flags implemented and exposed through admin API for global/org/route scope
Runtime adapter middleware implemented with feature toggle and unit+integration tests
Regression replayer extended to support streaming and tool-call captures and able to produce diff reports
Canary run executed with at least two paying customers and telemetry shows no functional regressions
Updated migration guide and deprecation plan published in Confluence and linked from console release notes

2025-02-18 - Design review: agreed to adapter shim approach; Design asked for example flows for SDK teams. Assigned follow-up to PM for SDK coordination.
2025-02-20 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike completed to measure CPU overhead of adapter. Observed ~2.8% p99 latency increase on test harness with 8k token streams. Will add sampling control to adapter config.

2025-02-25 - QA: Added integration tests for tool-call remapping and streaming frame fidelity. Two flaky tests identified; flakiness due to timing assumptions in test harness. Tracking as sub-issue ENG-49103.
